content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository lowRISC_ibex_pr1865, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
Observed Behavior
The core_busy_o output signal of the non-lockstep core is used to gate the core clock, which is used by the regular Ibex core and its lockstep counterpart.
ibex/rtl/ibex_top.sv
Lines 211 to 219 in 3943a4e
assign clock_en     = core_busy_q | debug_req_i | irq_pending | irq_nm_i;
assign core_sleep_o = ~clock_en;
prim_clock_gating core_clock_gate_i (
.clk_i    (clk_i),
.en_i     (clock_en),
.test_en_i(test_en_i),
.clk_o    (clk)
);
ibex/rtl/ibex_top.sv
Lines 286 to 287 in 3943a4e
) u_ibex_core (
.clk_i(clk),
ibex/rtl/ibex_top.sv
Lines 927 to 928 in 3943a4e
) u_ibex_lockstep (
.clk_i                  (clk),
This means that the lockstep core gets gated in the same clock cycle as the regular core, even though the lockstep core is a few cycles delayed. A low-glitch in the core_busy_o output of the non-lockstep core thus does not lead to a comparison mismatch and a major alert because the lockstep core is already clock-gated when it would produce the value of core_busy_o that is used in the comparison.
ibex/rtl/ibex_lockstep.sv
Lines 453 to 454 in 3943a4e
assign outputs_mismatch       = enable_cmp_q & (shadow_outputs_q != core_outputs_q[0]);
assign alert_major_internal_o = outputs_mismatch | shadow_alert_major_internal;
Expected Behavior
A low-glitch/mismatch in the core_busy_o output signal of the non-lockstep core should lead to a major alert by the lockstep core.
Steps to reproduce the issue
Run the chip_sw_ibex_lockstep_glitch test in OpenTitan (currently in lowRISC/opentitan#15221) and override port_idx to the index of core_busy_o in output_ports.

The root cause here is that in ibex_top.sv we’re using the single “core_busy_o” to gate both the regular and lock‐step cores, then in ibex_lockstep.sv we never see a glitch in core_busy_o (since the lock‐step core is already off) and thus no major‐alert is ever raised. To fix this we need to:

 1. Decouple the clock gating for the lock‐step core – update the clock‐enable logic in ibex_top.sv so the lock‐step core sees its own (possibly delayed) busy signal, not the direct non–lockstep core_busy_o.
 2. In ibex_lockstep.sv, ensure that any glitch on the gated‐off busy signal still propagates through your compare logic (or add an error-capture on the busy port).
 3. Potentially extend prim_clock_gating.sv (or add a variant) to allow transparent bypass or dedicated control for lock-step.
 4. If you’re indexing outputs by port_idx in a shared port-map (output_ports array), you’ll also need to update the definitions/indices in ibex_pkg.sv so the non–lockstep busy port and the lock‐step busy shadow port are distinct.

```  
ibex/rtl/ibex_top.sv  
ibex/rtl/ibex_lockstep.sv  
ibex/rtl/prim_clock_gating.sv  
ibex/rtl/ibex_pkg.sv  
```
